purpose: Concrete unresolved static investigations for later system-specific passes. Every entry here has a named starting point (a function address, table, or archive) -- none are generic 'investigate further' placeholders.

entries.description: Disassemble func_0018654C (called by both T_0018E4F4 and func_001AF768 immediately after func_001AD268) to learn what it does with the boxer-table classification result.

Structurally analyze xdbboxr.adf's decoded payload bytes from offset ~0x37 (just past the proven +0x18 flags array) through its 9704-byte end, looking for string data, a second record array, or further sub-headers.

Apply the +0x18 packed-2-bit-array model found for xdbboxr.adf to at least one other xdb table's own consumer function (accessor functions for xdbvenue/xdbalias/xdbevent/xdbhmtwn/xdbstore/xdbpref/xdbrivl/xdbtrain/xdbcutpn were only located, not disassembled, in either pass) to confirm or refute that the layout generalizes across the xdb family.

Locate the constructor/allocator for whatever object type has a +0x10 'next' field walked by func_00186464, and any function that writes to that field (list insertion). Neither was found in this pass.
Search for callers of func_001AF768 and T_0018E4F4 (one level up from where this pass stopped) to identify which UI screen(s) they construct.

Disassemble the 9 subsystem-init functions chained after func_001AF768's two boxer-table queries (func_00186954, func_001B9B58, func_001850C0, func_001A1D1C, func_001A90D8, func_001B8F08, func_001AC34C, func_001B6338, and one more) to learn what other subsystems this screen depends on.
entries.relevance: cross-subsystem dependency mapping / program-28 and others depending on which subsystems are found

entries.description: Trace the pointer at ELF virtual 0x6DE908 (a raw pointer to the 9-entry boxer-appearance-family registry table's base address, found in a data region) to whatever larger structure or function reads through it.

Locate the loader/dispatch function for preload/tables.viv (72 members: CSV tables plus hairstyle/lighting text files). No string xref to 'tables.viv' exists in BOOT.BIN's extracted string table; a raw-byte search (the same technique that found the registry table) was not yet performed for this specific name in isolation from the registry table's own listing.
Trace T_0033A614 (the sole function referencing 'bootpreloads.viv') further to learn its boot-preload dispatch logic, including whether it references the HK_*.bh / hk_*.viv family by name.

Search BOOT.BIN (already covered) and other PRX modules (not analyzed in any pass so far) for any reference to 'scrptpal.viv' or a runtime-constructed equivalent, and locate the call site using the '%s%s.viv' generic path-builder format string found near the registry table's string data.
entries.relevance: program-05/06 (fight-engine scripts), explicitly deferred out of Task 10/11 scope
